name: Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS)
surveyQuestion: Do you have any of these health conditions? (select all that apply) -> Irritable bowel syndrome (IBS). Check: Has a doctor told you that you have IBS? Yes, IBS-D (loose stools) / Yes, IBS-C (constipation) / Yes, IBS-mixed / Yes, not sure which type / Not sure (see a doctor) / No. Red-flag screen first: blood in stool, weight loss without trying, anaemia, night symptoms, new symptoms after age 50, fever, family history of colon cancer, coeliac disease or IBD.

waterMl.notes: No change from general range (topic 30: 2,500 ml men, 2,000 ml women); at least about 1,500-2,000 ml matters, especially in IBS-C; more in heat or loose stools (topic 31, cap 4,500, est.); severe diarrhoea needs a doctor; with kidney, heart or liver disease, pregnancy, fluid limit or diuretic show general range only. Follow your doctor's advice.

conflictsWith.rule: Coeliac disease overrides FODMAP wheat tolerance: strict gluten-free; test before dropping gluten (P19)
Use lactose-free swaps; lactose limit applies only if lactose is a trigger (P18)
No onion and garlic lowers FODMAP load, but pulses, iron and fibre need dietitian review (P33)
Pulses and soy are protein base but often high FODMAP; dietitian needed (P34)
Anaemia must be checked by a doctor before being attributed to IBS (P11)
No crash diets or skipped meals (P25)

warnings: IBS is diagnosed by a doctor; Rome IV criteria shown for information only
Red flags: blood in stool, weight loss, anaemia, night symptoms, onset after 50, fever, family history of colon cancer, coeliac disease or IBD: see a doctor before any diet plan
Low-FODMAP elimination is dietitian-led and time-limited (about 2-6 weeks), then reintroduce; not long term
Never advise medicines, peppermint capsules, probiotics, laxatives or fibre supplement doses
Test for coeliac disease before removing gluten
Follow your doctor's advice on fluids
